title: Vadstena Abbey

buildingCutout.basis: Named mapped church and its west choir.

terrainReference.basis: Original ground at the south of the two east-gable portals.

mapIdentity.provider: Named Vadstena Abbey Church, museum, Brothers’ Convent and surviving ruin walls in OpenStreetMap.
mapIdentity.scope: The named native church outline locates both long nave walls and the narrower west choir, with the neighbouring museum and hotel footprints fixing the ranges. The seven mapped fragments establish the layout of the low ruins west of the church.

note: The Qualla photographs establish the pale limestone east gable with buttresses, double-pitch slate roof and copper flèche, and the two stories and rows of red window frames of Munkklostret. The parish architectural survey identifies the west choir, sacristy, window form and portals. The state owner describes the materials and conservation of the nuns’ wings.
